statement: Start with one capable agent and add more agents only when complexity or tool overlap causes measured failures.
Tool or skill overlap is a stronger warning signal than raw catalogue count.
Agent Skills use catalogue metadata, activated SKILL.md instructions, then on-demand resources.
Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines and below about 5,000 tokens where practical; move conditional detail to references.
Use executable code for bounded filtering, joining, ranking, deduplication, aggregation, validation, and other exact work.
Use a skill when the model should decide how; use a workflow when order, checkpoints, side effects, or approvals must be controlled.
Subagents are useful for isolated context, specialist tools, or independent parallel work.
Copilot SDK custom-agent skills are injected in full when the agent starts and are not inherited by child agents.
Evaluate skills with structural gates, overlap checks, and with-skill versus without-skill live runs.
Blind A/B comparison reduces evaluator bias when comparing skill variants.
Pin architecture validators and fail when they are missing; optional silent gates do not provide reproducible proof.
MCP is a protocol boundary for external capabilities and context, not a replacement for every local function.
OKF can represent knowledge as Markdown plus metadata, but a guide may keep human-readable Markdown as its canonical source.
Headless harness adapters should make model, permissions, output format, persistence, and schema controls explicit.
Evaluate agent and workflow behavior with repeatable inputs, expected tools, stored results, and repeated runs where nondeterminism matters.
Treat skills, references, and bundled scripts as executable supply-chain inputs that require review, least privilege, sandboxing, and audit logs.
A reproducible headless run should make the model, permissions, persistence, output format, timeout, and working data explicit.
Large shared skill libraries can be filtered, deduplicated, and cached before exposure to a requesting agent.
